column1: # Ambient operator environment the sealed suite REFUSES to inherit.
# tests/run.sh unsets every name matched here before it admits a single test, so
# a behavior test sees only what it sets for itself. tests/fm-cloud-provider-seal.test.sh
# pins this file against run.sh and against an exact literal count, so the seal
# cannot be widened or narrowed without a visible diff.
# Two record kinds, both tab-separated:
#   exact<TAB>NAME<TAB>WHY
#   prefix<TAB>PREFIX<TAB>WHY
# WHY is not decoration. Each of these was measured, not guessed:
#   FM_HOME alone makes tests/fm-worker-lifecycle.test.sh non-deterministic. On
#   merged main, same commit, same machine: `env -i` plus PATH passes 36/36;
#   adding FM_HOME=<real operator home> fails the Azure provider refusal matrix;
#   a full operator shell fails the classification/admission matrix instead. The
#   failing unit VARIES between runs, which is the signature of a suite reading
#   real, changing operator state.
#   FM_WORKER_PROVIDER_COMMAND and the FM_AZURE_* identity together are how a
#   test that means to prove a REFUSAL instead provisioned a real billable VM
#   (vm-fm7c799d-wkr-01, 2026-08-20, task tag `cloud-noenv-c7`, a fixture id).
# Nothing under FM_TEST_ is sealed: that prefix is the runner's own contract with
# the test (FM_TEST_SKIP_HERDR, FM_TEST_HOST_CAPABILITIES_ABSENT, ...), and CI
# sets FM_PI_* deliberately.
exact
column3: the operator's real firstmate home; a suite that reads it reads live, changing controller state
